answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed fire-lookout tower on a named ridge, reached only by a weekly supply voyage up the valley past the mesa flats. The lookout logs every smoke sighting in a public register and must answer random radio checks live from the tower within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two towers. Each further identity on the same funding trail needs another tower, another season of live watch, and a license fee in outside money that doubles each time, so every extra fake costs another real tower, another human, and twice the prior fee.
